Take-Home Exercise 1:Survey Analysis of Informal Labourers’ Income

Author

Cheok En Qi

Published

February 8, 2026

Modified

February 13, 2026

Overview

This report analyses the income of informal rural labourers in the northern mountainous regions of Vietnam.

Data Preparation

pacman::p_load(
  tidyverse,
  readxl,
  janitor,
  ggthemes,
  patchwork,
  ggridges,
  scales
)
  
df_raw <- read_xlsx("chapthe/data/Upload for elsiver.xlsx")

df_raw <- clean_names(df_raw)

Data cleaning and prepartion

The dataset was cleaned and prepared before performing data visualization and analysis

Categorical variables for example, province, gender, education, training and credit access were converted into factor variables

Continuous measures for example income were also converted to numeric format to ensure accurate plotting.

Likert-scale items were also converted to numeric values

Invalid entries were also set to NA to exclude them from the data

df <- df_raw

# Categorical variables converted factor
df$cpro <- factor(df$cpro)
df$cgen <- factor(df$cgen)
df$crac <- factor(df$crac)
df$cjob <- factor(df$cjob)
df$cqui <- factor(df$cqui)

df$fedu <- factor(df$fedu)
df$fvtp <- factor(df$fvtp)
df$fcra <- factor(df$fcra)
df$ftap <- factor(df$ftap)


# Numeric / continuous variables
df$tein <- as.numeric(df$tein)
df$tain <- as.numeric(df$tain)
df$tsii <- as.numeric(df$tsii)
df$toin <- as.numeric(df$toin)
df$lcre <- as.numeric(df$lcre)
df$lsav <- as.numeric(df$lsav)
df$lwda <- as.numeric(df$lwda)


# Likert-scale converted to numeric
df$ppo1 <- as.numeric(df$ppo1)
df$ppo2 <- as.numeric(df$ppo2)
df$ppo3 <- as.numeric(df$ppo3)
df$ppo4 <- as.numeric(df$ppo4)
df$ppo5 <- as.numeric(df$ppo5)

df$aro1 <- as.numeric(df$aro1)
df$aro2 <- as.numeric(df$aro2)
df$aro3 <- as.numeric(df$aro3)
df$aro4 <- as.numeric(df$aro4)
df$aro5 <- as.numeric(df$aro5)


# convert to NA
df$aro2[df$aro2 > 3] <- NA


#final cleaned dataset
df$income <- df$tein

Visualisation 1 — Income Distribution

NoteVisualisation 1 — Income Distribution
  • Visual
  • Code
ggplot(df, aes(x = income)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 30, color = "white") +
  labs(title = "Income Distribution", x = "Income", y = "Count") +
  theme_minimal()

Observation:
Income is right-skewed. Most labourers fall within lower income brackets while only a small proportion earn substantially higher incomes, indicating inequality in earnings.

Visualisation 2 — Income by Province Group (CPRO)

NoteVisualisation 2 — Income by Province Group (CPRO)
  • Visual
  • Code
ggplot(df, aes(cpro, income)) +
  geom_boxplot(fill = "steelblue") +
  labs(title = "Income by Province Group",
       x = "Province",
       y = "Income") +
  theme_minimal()

Observation:
Income levels differ across provinces, suggesting regional variation in job opportunities and economic development.

Visualisation 3 — Income by Education Level

NoteVisualisation 3 — Income by Education Level
  • Visual
  • Code
ggplot(df, aes(fedu, income)) +
  geom_boxplot(fill = "steelblue") +
  labs(title = "Income by Education Level",
       x = "Education Level",
       y = "Income") +
  theme_minimal()

Observation:
Higher education categories tend to have higher median incomes, indicating that education improves earning potential.

Visualisation 4 — Income by Credit Access

NoteVisualisation 4 — Income by Credit Access
  • Visual
  • Code
df_credit <- df |> drop_na(fcra, income)

ggplot(df_credit, aes(fcra, income)) +
  geom_boxplot(fill = "steelblue") +
  labs(title = "Income by Credit Access",
       x = "Credit Access",
       y = "Income") +
  theme_minimal()

Observation:
Respondents with access to credit generally report slightly higher median incomes, suggesting financial access may facilitate business expansion or improved employment opportunities.

Visualisation 5 — Income vs Savings

NoteVisualisation 5 — Income vs Savings
  • Visual
  • Code
df_scatter <- df |> drop_na(income, lsav)

ggplot(df_scatter, aes(income, lsav)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.4) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm") +
  labs(title = "Income vs Savings",
       x = "Income",
       y = "Savings") +
  theme_minimal()

Observation:
Savings increase as income rises, indicating a positive linear relationship between earning capacity and savings ability.

Visualisation 6 — Income by Gender and Training

NoteVisualisation 6 — Income by Gender and Training
  • Visual
  • Code
p1 <- ggplot(df, aes(cgen, income)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  theme_minimal()

p2 <- ggplot(df, aes(fvtp, income)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  theme_minimal()

p1 + p2

Observation:
Income differences across gender and training status are modest with overlapping distributions.

Visualisation 7 — Likert Response Distribution (PPO1 & ARO4)

NoteVisualisation 7 — Likert Response Distribution (PPO1 & ARO4)
  • Visual
  • Code
p1 <- df |> 
  drop_na(ppo1) |> 
  count(ppo1) |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = "", y = n, fill = factor(ppo1))) +
  geom_col(position = "fill") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format()) +
  labs(title = "PPO1 Response Distribution",
       x = NULL,
       y = "Share",
       fill = "Score") +
  theme_minimal()

p2 <- df |> 
  drop_na(aro4) |> 
  count(aro4) |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = "", y = n, fill = factor(aro4))) +
  geom_col(position = "fill") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format()) +
  labs(title = "ARO4 Response Distribution",
       x = NULL,
       y = "Share",
       fill = "Score") +
  theme_minimal()

p1 + p2

Observation:
Responses cluster around mid-to-high scores, indicating generally positive perceptions.

Visualisation 8 — PPO Correlation Heatmap

NoteVisualisation 8 — PPO Correlation Heatmap
  • Visual
  • Code
ppo_vars <- c("ppo1","ppo2","ppo3","ppo4","ppo5")

df_ppo <- df |> 
  select(all_of(ppo_vars)) |> 
  drop_na()

corr_mat <- cor(df_ppo, method = "spearman")

corr_long <- as.data.frame(as.table(corr_mat))
colnames(corr_long) <- c("Var1", "Var2", "Rho")

ggplot(corr_long, aes(x = Var1, y = Var2, fill = Rho)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white") +
  scale_fill_gradient2(midpoint = 0, limits = c(-1, 1)) +
  labs(title = "Spearman Correlation Among PPO Likert Items",
       x = NULL,
       y = NULL,
       fill = "ρ") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1),
        panel.grid = element_blank())

Observation:
The PPO items show moderate positive correlations, indicating related but distinct perceptions.
